title: Enterprises self-host open-weight code models over hosted China APIs by Q2 2027
body: GLM-5.2's fully-open MIT release is the inflection that turns the open-weight coding-model trend into a data-sovereignty decision rather than just a price-performance one. The weights are publicly downloadable and run on local or virtual-machine hardware, and the surrounding stack now makes self-hosting practical at scale: vLLM v0.23.0 promotes its faster execution path to default for dense models, and MosaicQuant's unified 4-bit scheme reports near-FP16 accuracy, cutting the memory and cost of running a 753B mixture-of-experts yourself. The same coverage that praises the model's price-performance flags the catch: routing requests through Z.ai's hosted API carries China-jurisdiction data-handling considerations that enterprises with sensitive code and regulated data must weigh. That splits the buying decision in two - you can take the open weights and run them inside your own boundary, or consume the convenient hosted API and accept foreign data jurisdiction. The prediction is that within roughly three quarters this hardens into an explicit posture: at least one named enterprise, regulated-sector buyer, or developer-tooling framework publishes guidance or a default that prefers self-hosting permissively-licensed open weights over a foreign-hosted inference API specifically on data-jurisdiction or sovereignty grounds, treating where-the-inference-runs as a procurement control rather than an afterthought. The catalyst is a top-tier open-weight coding model that is genuinely self-hostable arriving at the same moment cheap 4-bit serving removes the deployment tax; the same data-sovereignty thread runs through this month's Confidential Computing Summit agenda. The counter-risk is that managed convenience and tooling integrations keep most teams on the hosted API despite the jurisdiction flag, leaving self-hosting a regulated-sector niche rather than a published default.

reasoning.because: GLM-5.2 ships self-hostable MIT weights; its hosted Z.ai API flags China data-jurisdiction handling
reasoning.given: Cheap 4-bit serving (MosaicQuant) plus vLLM defaults make running the weights yourself a real option
reasoning.so_that: Enterprises codify a self-host-the-weights, avoid-the-foreign-hosted-API posture for sensitive-code data sovereignty
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; >=1 enterprise/framework self-host policy cites data jurisdiction
reasoning.plain_language: A top free Chinese AI coder is now downloadable. Firms worried where their code data goes will run it in-house, not its cloud.

summary: GLM-5.2's open MIT weights are self-hostable, while its hosted Z.ai API carries China data-jurisdiction concerns, and cheaper 4-bit serving makes self-hosting practical. Expect an enterprise or dev-tooling framework to publish a self-host-over-foreign-API policy on sovereignty grounds by Q2 2027.
